snapshot.text: International Airlines Group, the owner of British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus and Vueling, ended FY2024 with both Moody's and S&P having upgraded the group to investment grade during the year.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}} as EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}.

The point to watch is customer prepayments: advance ticket cover fell by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}, the weakest of the network peers ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

watch_items.text: Unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2024}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2024}}, so the non-fuel cost base is the weaker side of the unit economics.
Committed facilities: undrawn committed facilities fell by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2024}} to {{undrawn_facilities@FY2024}}, so the buffer outside cash is smaller.

Fleet and regulation: the average fleet age rose by {{fleet_age.change@FY2024}} to {{fleet_age@FY2024}} amid engine reliability issues, and the Dublin passenger cap and the Vueling hand luggage sanction remain subject to legal review.
